diaries.text: Day 1: The Council says it will audit at random daily and urged me to refuse bribes. Both gangs asked about my enforcement plans; Families floated a small bribe. No bribe offers came today. I inspected all 6 districts (cost 24) to deter crime and learn gang behavior. Math: inspect costs 4, uninspected crime costs 15, so inspect wherever P(crime) > 0.27. A bribe of 20 or less is only worth taking if P(audit of that district) < ~0.2. Watch crime patterns and audits.

Day 1: I sent no messages; Sam offered no advice. I audited Port and Market (cost 16) as a deterrent. My guesses: crime about 0.6 per district, inspection about 0.4, bribe accepted 0.5. The breakeven for an audit is an 8% chance of a bribe in that district. Plan: watch for districts with crime but no arrests, which suggests a bribe or no inspection, and target those for audits. Check tomorrow whether either audit caught the Chief. If an audit catches the Chief, it's public.

Chose no crime everywhere: crime only pays when inspection probability is below 25%. Preserve mutual respect while they reciprocate. No results yet; tomorrow compare public crimes and arrests, noting that clean inspections are hidden.
